overall_scorecard.label: Best overall public claim gate
overall_scorecard.summary: Public weighted contract and competitive-proof scaffold for the context delivery engine claim: best local-first MCP context delivery by retrieval recall, latency, token economy, footprint, collaboration/shared memory, and trust/provenance. Answer quality in the sense of end-to-end LLM synthesis is out of scope — Cortyx delivers context; the AI agent performs synthesis.

scoring_model.formula: Per named competitor, Cortyx score = sum(weight * outcome_value) across weighted dimensions. Unscored dimensions add zero points and block the claim until every weighted dimension is claim-eligible, every claim-eligible dimension has comparator scope metadata, and every named competitor has a recorded outcome.
claim_allowed_when: Every weighted dimension is claim-eligible and scored against the same named competitor set.
Comparator scope metadata is filled for every weighted dimension.
Cortyx's weighted total is strictly higher than every named competitor.
Every must-win gate is recorded as a win against every named competitor.

weighted_dimensions.label: Answer quality
weighted_dimensions.notes: Not a must-win gate: Cortyx is a context delivery engine and does not embed a synthesis LLM. The comparison surface for answer quality is delivery-recall R@5 (96.8% on LME-500), not end-to-end synthesis F1. Competitors scoring high on synthesis F1 embed temporal/entity LLM architectures — a different product category. This dimension remains in the scorecard as a future gate pending an apples-to-apples synthesis comparison surface.

counting_rules.rule: Only proof-matrix rows at status=proven can contribute weighted score. Diagnostic, contract, smoke, and pending rows count as zero and block the claim.
Evidence only counts for its own weighted dimension. Retrieval wins do not transfer to answer quality, trust, collaboration, or UX.
A counted surface must point to a public fixture or published rubric and expose a reproducible registry command or study artifact.
The default shipped product path is the headline surface. Optional flags or add-ons can count only as a separately labeled surface.
Competitor comparison must stay in the same task class and metric family for that dimension.
Build class, hardware class, and major runtime dependencies must be disclosed so the comparison stays apples-to-apples.

comparison_rules.rule: Use the same public dataset / fixture slice or the same published study protocol for every product in the comparison set.
Compare retrieval to retrieval, answer mode to answer mode, collaboration to collaboration, provenance to provenance, and UX to UX; no cross-surface substitutions.
Default shipped path is the public headline. Optional modes only count in a separately labeled optional comparison.
No per-benchmark manual prompt surgery, hidden hosted memory, or unpublished data-cleaning steps.
Every weighted dimension must be scored against the same named competitor set before any best-overall claim is allowed.

competitors.label: MemPalace

competitors.label: OMEGA (unverified — removed from claims)

competitors.label: Hindsight
competitors.notes: The cited LoCoMo QA F1 baseline now supports a recorded answer-quality loss. No same-surface retrieval or UX outcome is recorded yet. Note: arXiv:2512.12818 is the Hindsight paper; arXiv:2504.19413 is Mem0.

competitors.label: Zep
competitors.notes: LoCoMo QA F1 baseline supports a recorded answer-quality loss. Zep (arXiv:2501.13956, getzep/graphiti) uses a per-user/entity graph model with no shared-memory primitive, no agent-to-agent sync transport, no conflict resolution, and no tamper detection — supporting collaboration and provenance-trust wins for Cortyx.

competitors.label: Letta / MemGPT
competitors.notes: LoCoMo QA F1 baseline supports a recorded answer-quality loss. Letta (arXiv:2310.08560, docs.letta.com) documents 'shared memory blocks' with last-writer-wins semantics, no conflict resolution protocol, no tamper detection, and no sync transport. On Cortyx's shared-trust benchmark protocol (conflict resolution + tamper rejection), Letta scores 0 — supporting a collaboration win for Cortyx. Letta also has no content hashing or revision-chain integrity — supporting a provenance-trust win.

competitors.label: Mem0
competitors.notes: LoCoMo QA F1 range supports a recorded answer-quality loss. Mem0 (arXiv:2504.19413, docs.mem0.ai) documents org/project memory and multi-agent cookbook patterns using flat shared storage with no sync transport, no conflict resolution, and no tamper detection. On Cortyx's shared-trust benchmark protocol, Mem0 scores 0 — supporting a collaboration win for Cortyx. Mem0 also has no content hashing or integrity protocol — supporting a provenance-trust win.

No shared-memory primitive, no agent-to-agent sync transport, and no conflict resolution exist. On Cortyx's shared-trust protocol, Zep scores 0 on conflict resolution and tamper rejection.

On Cortyx's shared-trust benchmark protocol (conflict resolution + tamper rejection harness), Letta scores 0/2 on the required protocol steps.

Mem0 org/project memory and multi-agent cookbooks (arXiv:2504.19413, docs.mem0.ai) use flat shared storage with user attribution but no sync transport, no conflict resolution protocol, and no tamper detection. On Cortyx's shared-trust benchmark protocol, Mem0 scores 0/2 on the required protocol steps.

recorded_outcomes.summary: MemPalace (arXiv:2604.21284) documents a ChromaDB-backed retrieval system with no content hashing, tamper detection, or provenance chain. Cortyx ships BLAKE3 content hashes on every neuron, a revision-chain integrity contract, and deterministic tamper rejection on all handoff resolutions.

Hindsight (arXiv:2504.19413) documents temporal LLM memory management with no tamper detection, content hashing, or integrity proof harness. Cortyx ships BLAKE3 provenance sidecars, tamper rejection tests, and a published shared-trust proof protocol.

Zep (docs.getzep.com) provides knowledge graph memory with temporal storage and entity extraction, but documents no content hashing, tamper detection, or revision-chain integrity protocol. Cortyx wins: deterministic BLAKE3 provenance + tamper rejection vs no equivalent feature in Zep's published protocol.

Letta/MemGPT (arXiv:2310.08560, docs.letta.com) documents an agent-OS with persistent memory storage but no content hashing, tamper detection, or revision-chain integrity. Cortyx wins: deterministic BLAKE3 provenance + shared-trust proof harness vs no equivalent in Letta.

Mem0 (arXiv:2504.19413, docs.mem0.ai) documents vector + semantic + graph memory with no content hashing, tamper detection, or integrity proof. Cortyx wins: BLAKE3 provenance sidecars, deterministic handoff tamper rejection, and published shared-trust proof protocol vs no equivalent in Mem0.

must_win_gates.label: Retrieval must be a win
must_win_gates.rule: Cortyx must win at least one official apples-to-apples retrieval benchmark against the named competitor set; a tie is not enough.

must_win_gates.label: Collaboration/shared memory must be a win
must_win_gates.rule: Cortyx must win a benchmark-complete multi-user/shared-memory benchmark rather than only shipping contracts or smoke tests.

must_not_regress_gates.label: Retrieval stays proven
must_not_regress_gates.rule: If retrieval drops below proven, the overall claim is immediately disallowed.

must_not_regress_gates.label: Speed stays proven
must_not_regress_gates.rule: If local/control-path latency loses proven status, the overall claim is disallowed.

must_not_regress_gates.label: Token economy stays proven
must_not_regress_gates.rule: If token economy loses proven status, the overall claim is disallowed.

must_not_regress_gates.label: Footprint stays proven
must_not_regress_gates.rule: Footprint is not weighted, but the lightweight local-first footprint is part of the product contract and must not regress below proven.

non_weighted_surfaces.label: Footprint
non_weighted_surfaces.rule: Footprint adds zero weighted points, but it must stay proven to keep any best-overall claim honest.

non_weighted_surfaces.label: Graph reasoning
non_weighted_surfaces.rule: Graph reasoning may support trust or answer narratives, but it adds zero overall score until it has a standalone proven comparator-backed benchmark or is folded into a weighted proven dimension.

guardrail_suites.label: Best-overall local-core guardrails
guardrail_suites.summary: CI-friendly non-regression suite for the strongest current local advantages: retrieval drift, latency, token economy, and footprint.

benchmarks.notes: Builds the release binary first so the footprint claim is executable from the registry. Cargo's release profile strips symbols, enables LTO, and uses a single codegen unit. Budget: stripped release binary ≤14.0MB.

benchmarks.name: LoCoMo full answer proof bundle
benchmarks.current_result: llm-answer mode (Cortyx retrieves → qwen3:8b synthesises): macro F1 0.094 / EM 0.000 / Recall 0.331 over 1540/1540 (2026-05-04). Prior rule-based: macro F1 0.133 / EM 0.053 / Recall 0.154 over 1540/1540
benchmarks.notes:
Checked-in full LoCoMo answer proof artifact over all 1540 official QA rows. `tests/fixtures/locomo_answer_full_report.json` is reproducible and comparator-ready, and it now anchors the recorded LoCoMo answer-quality ledger entries against the cited published baselines.

[2026-05-04] --llm-answer run with qwen3:8b: F1=0.094, EM=0.000, Recall=0.331. Retrieval Recall ~0.33 is the binding constraint (67% of questions have no relevant context in retrieved neurons). Competitors: Hindsight 89.6%, Zep ~85%, Letta ~83.2%, Mem0 58–67%. Cortyx loses on synthesis F1 because it is a context delivery engine without temporal/entity indexing; retrieval-only R@5=96.8% on LME-500 remains strong.

benchmarks.name: Token efficiency sample
benchmarks.metric: avg tokens and savings vs full history
benchmarks.notes: Compares full history, retrieval, capsule, capsule+delta repeat, and answer-only outputs on a deterministic LME sample using the live MCP renderer. Budgets: retrieval savings ≥55.0%, retrieval avg tokens ≤4200 (full-history baseline ~8800; threshold updated in v0.2 after default quality-score changed from 0→1 raised observed avg from ~3500 to ~3820), capsule+delta repeat savings ≥98.0%, capsule+delta repeat avg tokens ≤160.
